Glossary

## brahman ब्रह्मन्

the ground and totality of what is

Sanskrit · glossed in English

[Glossary](https://www.philosophydef.com/glossary) / brahman

A term is not a word. It is a working part of somebody's argument, and the English word usually offered for it is a compromise. This page gives the compromise, the argument, and the reading the sources do not support.

Where it is filed: [God](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/god) · [Being](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/being) · [Eternity](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/eternity) · [Existence](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/existence) · [Understanding](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/understanding) · [Spirit](https://www.philosophydef.com/themes/spirit)

### What the term does

Brahman names the ultimate reality in the Upaniṣads — the source of the world, that from which things arise and into which they return, and the object of the knowledge the texts are meant to transmit. The etymology relates it to growth and expansion. The Advaita reading treats brahman as without distinctions, so that the plurality of things is a matter of appearance at the level of ignorance; Rāmānuja and others insist that the world is real and related to brahman as body to self. How the two are related is the principal division in Vedānta.

### The reading the sources do not support

Rendered as 'God', which brings in creation, will, and personality from the Abrahamic vocabulary. In the Advaita reading brahman is impersonal and does not create so much as appear as the world.
